title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene hazards, vital signs and rapid-response decisions test whether you can think clearly when every clue matters.

landing.intro: Scene hazards, vital signs, emergency maths and calm judgement. Can you think clearly when every clue matters?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge explores entrance-level paramedic knowledge across 40 varied questions. It covers anatomy and physiology, emergency numeracy, observation trends, scene safety, calm communication, handover and multi-clue prioritisation.

The five challenges become progressively more applied, moving from accessible dispatch foundations into body systems, scene judgement, competing priorities and a final integrated response. Questions use worldwide principles rather than country-specific protocols or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the response areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for paramedic practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Work through each response challenge at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose the single option best supported by the visible clues. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal.
Keep going as the decisions become harder, then reveal your score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited paramedic entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Emergency procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local guidance and appropriately qualified emergency professionals.

profile-1.title: The Emergency Standout
profile-1.copy: You combined excellent foundational knowledge with calm, evidence-led judgement across the entire response assessment. Scene hazards, changing observations and communication details stayed clear even when the final cases became demanding.

profile-2.title: The Rapid-Response Natural
profile-2.copy: You showed a strong feel for the knowledge and judgement behind safe emergency response. Most of the assessment's trend, numeracy, safety and handover traps did not pull you off course.

profile-3.title: The Calm Scene Solver
profile-3.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, scene decisions and multi-clue cases with steady reasoning. A few finer handover and observation details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profile-4.title: The Steady Responder
profile-4.copy: You built a solid result by following visible evidence and treating safety seriously. Your strongest area shows where your emergency-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profile-5.title: The Promising Candidate
profile-5.copy: You solved a good share of the assessment and showed useful instincts across several response areas. The answer review will reveal which foundations are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The First-Response Explorer
profile-6.copy: The assessment uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, safety-first judgement. Every reviewed answer is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind calm emergency thinking.

paramedic-r1q4.question: A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?
answers: Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe

paramedic-r4q1.question: A person is beside moving traffic with no protected working area. What is safest?
answers: Keep clear, identify the danger and seek appropriate scene support
Walk into traffic and wave vehicles around

paramedic-r4q4.question: A task may expose the face and hands to splashing body fluid. What guides PPE choice?
answers: The colour of the equipment bag

paramedic-r6q5.question: A coughing person is sharing a small waiting area. Which general safety action fits the visible risk?
answers: Turn off all ventilation without assessment

visual.ariaLabel: Vehicle stopped, two people, strong fuel smell

paramedic-r9q4.question: Which detail is most urgent to hand over?
answers: The fuel smell and possible ignition hazard

paramedic-r6q2.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?
answers: Repeat the same explanation more slowly
Ask, ‘Do you understand?’ and continue if they say yes
Shorten the explanation but keep the same terminology
Use plain words and check back

paramedic-r4q5.question: A bystander starts discussing a person's private details where others can hear. What is best?
answers: Move the conversation to a private setting and share only necessary information
Repeat the details so everyone understands
Post the information on a public notice

paramedic-r6q3.question: Someone needs to discuss a sensitive health concern. What protects dignity?
answers: Ask them to explain in front of everyone
Find a private setting and listen without making assumptions
Tell nearby people the concern first

paramedic-r6q1.question: A person says, “I'm terrified.” Which response is best?
answers: There is nothing to be scared about
Try not to think about it
I guarantee everything will be fine
I can see this is frightening. Tell me what worries you most

paramedic-r10q5.context: The person says, “I do not want this discussed where others can hear, and I still do not understand why you are asking.”
paramedic-r10q5.question: Which response protects privacy and checks understanding?
answers: Continue the discussion where everyone can hear
Avoid explaining and ask the same questions again
Move to an appropriate private setting, explain plainly and check understanding
Ask a bystander to explain on your behalf

paramedic-r2q6.context: The person's chest is moving, but very little air movement can be detected and they cannot speak normally.
paramedic-r2q6.question: Which concern has the highest priority?
answers: A possible airway or breathing problem needing immediate qualified assessment

paramedic-r5q6.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
paramedic-r5q6.question: Who needs attention first?
answers: Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
Person A, because their observations were recorded first

paramedic-r7q1.question: Which new information should change the response most?
